Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

args.command:
(PORT=3123 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1 && cat /tmp/server.log
echo "--- add book"
curl -s -i -X POST localhost:3123/books --data-urlencode "title=The Left Hand of Darkness" --data-urlencode "author=Ursula K. Le Guin" --data-urlencode "notes=Chapter 3 so far" | grep -i '^location'
ID=$(curl -s -i -X POST localhost:3123/books --data-urlencode "title=Piranesi" --data-urlencode "author=Susanna Clarke" | grep -i '^location' | sed 's/.*\/books\///' | tr -d '\r')
echo "second id: $ID"
echo "--- finish second from home"
curl -s -i -X POST "localhost:3123/books/$ID/finish?back=home" | grep -i '^location'
echo "--- home page lists"
curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -E 'class="title"|finished|Mark finished' 
echo "--- book page"
curl -s localhost:3123/books/$ID | grep -E '<h1>|by |Share|badge'
echo "--- JSON on disk"
cat data/books.json
echo "--- restart"
pkill -f "node server.mjs"; sleep 0.5
(PORT=3123 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -c 'class="title"'
pkill -f "node server.mjs"

args.content:
# My Books

A tiny book tracker. No accounts, no database — books are saved to `data/books.json`.

```sh
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

Set `PORT` to change the port and `BOOKS_FILE` to change where the JSON is stored.

## What it does

- `/` shows what you're currently reading, what you've finished, and a form to add a book.
- Each book has its own page at `/books/<id>` with title, author, notes (editable), and a
  "Mark finished" button. That URL is the link to share.

events.content:
The book tracker is done and working. Run it with `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

## What you get

- **Home page (`/`)** shows two lists — *Currently reading* and *Finished* — plus an "Add a book" form (title, author, notes). Each book in the reading list has a "Mark finished" button right there.
- **Book page (`/books/<id>`)** shows the title, author, when you started it, and your notes (which you can edit and save). It has a "Mark finished" button and a read-only "Share this book" field with the full URL — that page is the link you send to someone.
- **Storage** is `data/books.json`, written atomically (temp file + rename) so a crash mid-write can't corrupt it. The file is created on first add and reloaded on startup.

## How it's built

There are no dependencies beyond Node itself — the workspace had no web framework installed, and Node's built-in `http` module is plenty for four routes. Pages are server-rendered HTML with plain forms, so there's no client-side JavaScript to maintain.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `server.mjs` | Entry point; reads `PORT` and `BOOKS_FILE` env vars |
| `src/store.mjs` | Loads/saves the JSON file; add, finish, update notes |
| `src/app.mjs` | Request routing and form handling |
| `src/views.mjs` | HTML templates (all user input is escaped) |
| `test/` | 14 vitest tests covering the store and the HTTP routes |

## Verified

All 14 tests pass (`npm test`). I also ran the real server, added two books through the HTTP form endpoint, marked one finished, checked both pages rendered correctly, then restarted the server and confirmed both books came back with their status intact. Test data has been removed and `data/` is in `.gitignore` so your reading list won't end up in commits.

One small addition beyond what you asked: notes are editable from the book page, since a notes field you can only fill in once at creation seemed unlikely to be what you'd actually want. Nothing is committed yet — the changes are sitting in the working tree.

The book tracker is done and working. Run it with `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

## What you get

- **Home page (`/`)** shows two lists — *Currently reading* and *Finished* — plus an "Add a book" form (title, author, notes). Each book in the reading list has a "Mark finished" button right there.
- **Book page (`/books/<id>`)** shows the title, author, when you started it, and your notes (which you can edit and save). It has a "Mark finished" button and a read-only "Share this book" field with the full URL — that page is the link you send to someone.
- **Storage** is `data/books.json`, written atomically (temp file + rename) so a crash mid-write can't corrupt it. The file is created on first add and reloaded on startup.

## How it's built

There are no dependencies beyond Node itself — the workspace had no web framework installed, and Node's built-in `http` module is plenty for four routes. Pages are server-rendered HTML with plain forms, so there's no client-side JavaScript to maintain.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `server.mjs` | Entry point; reads `PORT` and `BOOKS_FILE` env vars |
| `src/store.mjs` | Loads/saves the JSON file; add, finish, update notes |
| `src/app.mjs` | Request routing and form handling |
| `src/views.mjs` | HTML templates (all user input is escaped) |
| `test/` | 14 vitest tests covering the store and the HTTP routes |

## Verified

All 14 tests pass (`npm test`). I also ran the real server, added two books through the HTTP form endpoint, marked one finished, checked both pages rendered correctly, then restarted the server and confirmed both books came back with their status intact. Test data has been removed and `data/` is in `.gitignore` so your reading list won't end up in commits.

One small addition beyond what you asked: notes are editable from the book page, since a notes field you can only fill in once at creation seemed unlikely to be what you'd actually want. Nothing is committed yet — the changes are sitting in the working tree.

shellCommands.command: ls -la && cat package.json 2>/dev/null; cat package-lock.json 2>/dev/null | head -30; node --version; npm --version

(PORT=3123 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1 && cat /tmp/server.log
echo "--- add book"
curl -s -i -X POST localhost:3123/books --data-urlencode "title=The Left Hand of Darkness" --data-urlencode "author=Ursula K. Le Guin" --data-urlencode "notes=Chapter 3 so far" | grep -i '^location'
ID=$(curl -s -i -X POST localhost:3123/books --data-urlencode "title=Piranesi" --data-urlencode "author=Susanna Clarke" | grep -i '^location' | sed 's/.*\/books\///' | tr -d '\r')
echo "second id: $ID"
echo "--- finish second from home"
curl -s -i -X POST "localhost:3123/books/$ID/finish?back=home" | grep -i '^location'
echo "--- home page lists"
curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -E 'class="title"|finished|Mark finished' 
echo "--- book page"
curl -s localhost:3123/books/$ID | grep -E '<h1>|by |Share|badge'
echo "--- JSON on disk"
cat data/books.json
echo "--- restart"
pkill -f "node server.mjs"; sleep 0.5
(PORT=3123 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -c 'class="title"'
pkill -f "node server.mjs"

pgrep -f "server.mjs" | xargs -r kill; sleep 0.3
PORT=3123 node server.mjs > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!
sleep 1
echo "books listed after restart: $(curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -c 'class="title"')"
kill $SERVER_PID
rm -rf data
ls data 2>/dev/null; cat /tmp/server.log; pgrep -fa server.mjs || echo "no server running"

sleep 1; echo "books listed after restart: $(curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -c 'class="title"')"; curl -s localhost:3123/ | grep -A1 'class="title"' | grep -oE '>[^<]+|finished [A-Za-z0-9, ]+|Mark finished'
npx vitest run 2>&1 | tail -4 && git status --short
